questions.text: Is the fan unplugged from the wall outlet right now?
Looking at the power switch, is it set to On or Off?
Have you confirmed another device works in this same outlet? (Do not test the fan while inspecting the plug.)
Do you see cracks, burn marks, or exposed wires on the plug or cord?
Have you noticed burning smell, sparking, or shock from this fan?

safeChecks.title: Confirm unplugged before any touch inspection
instructions: Make sure the power cord is disconnected from the wall.
Do not proceed with physical inspection while the fan is plugged in.

safeChecks.title: Visually inspect the plug (look only)
instructions: With the fan unplugged, look at the plug for cracks or burn marks.
Do not insert anything into the outlet or bend the prongs.

safeChecks.title: Verify switch position
instructions: With the fan unplugged, confirm whether the switch is Off or On.
If it is Off, that may explain why the fan will not run — this is not a confirmed diagnosis.

safeChecks.title: Check grille for visible blockage
instructions: With power disconnected, look at the grille for dust, fabric, or objects blocking airflow.
Only clear loose external debris you can reach without opening the fan.
Do not remove the grille, open the housing, or touch internal parts.

stopConditions.userMessage: Stop. Burning smell, sparking, or shock means this is out of scope for a home first-check. Unplug if safe and contact a qualified technician.
Possible damaged cord or plug. Do not use the fan. Contact a qualified technician.
Visible evidence is not enough to continue safely. The cause is not confirmed. Stop and contact a qualified technician.

escalationDefaults.message: The cause is not confirmed. Unplug the device and inspect only visible external damage — or stop and contact a qualified technician if anything looks unsafe.
